one_line.text: American physician, lifestyle-medicine advocate, and nutrition communicator who founded NutritionFacts.org and argues for whole-food, plant-predominant diets.

biography.text: Greger studied biology at Cornell and earned an M.D. from Tufts. He has worked in public-health and lifestyle-medicine communication and founded the nonprofit NutritionFacts.org, which publishes referenced nutrition videos and articles without advertising or product sponsorship. He says his grandmother's improvement after a low-fat plant-based diet and walking programme shaped his career.

background.text: His main work is large-scale synthesis and public explanation of nutrition, food safety, chronic-disease prevention, and lifestyle research rather than laboratory ageing research. He is a Fellow and diplomate in lifestyle medicine and has spent more than two decades advocating diet as a major modifiable cause of disease.

expertise.text: Greger is medically trained and highly experienced at searching, explaining, and popularising nutrition literature. He is not a registered dietitian, geriatrician, biogerontology researcher, or the clinician responsible for an individual reader. His strongest contribution is broad evidence discovery and behaviour-oriented explanation; personalised nutrition, frailty, medication, and disease management require additional expertise.

perspective_and_limits.text: Greger openly advocates a whole-food plant-based diet and tends to interpret a very large literature through that prior position. The volume of citations improves traceability but does not prevent selective emphasis, equal treatment of weak and strong designs, or extrapolation from cells, animals, biomarkers, and observational associations. His scepticism towards supplements and commercial anti-ageing claims is useful; his own dietary conclusions need the same adversarial standard.
